hints.text: As $x \to 3$ the bottom goes to $0$ while the top goes to $4$, so the quotient becomes enormous. The only question left is its sign.
From the right, $x$ is a bit more than $3$, so $x - 3$ is a tiny positive number. Decide the sign of a positive top over a tiny positive bottom.
The quotient is positive and grows without bound, so $\lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = +\infty$, which is choice A.

explanation: Test values just right of $3$: at $x = 3.01$ the quotient is $\frac{4.01}{0.01} = 401$, and at $x = 3.001$ it is $\frac{4.001}{0.001} = 4001$.
The top stays near $4$ (positive) while the bottom is a positive number shrinking to $0$.
The quotient grows without bound in the positive direction, so the limit is $+\infty$, choice A. From the left it would be $-\infty$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sign chart in one line
steps: Write the sign of each factor just to the right of $3$: top $(x + 1)$ is $+$, bottom $(x - 3)$ is $+$.
$\frac{+}{+} = +$, and the bottom is heading to $0$, so the size is infinite.
Infinite plus sign: $+\infty$. Do the same just left of $3$ and the bottom flips to $-$, giving $-\infty$.
